segments.text: Hey everyone, today I'm walking through my full editing workflow from import to export.
First I sort all footage into a project folder with subfolders for a-roll, b-roll, audio and graphics.
Then I do a rough cut on the timeline, removing pauses and anything that drags.
A lot of you ask about my voice, so here it is: I record voiceover on a dynamic microphone about four inches away.
It goes into a simple audio interface, and I add light compression and a high-pass filter in the edit.
Next comes b-roll. I lay it over the a-roll and keep each shot under four seconds.
Color grading is three steps for me: fix exposure and white balance first, then contrast.
I keep saturation natural here because skin tones break easily.
Last step is a creative LUT at about thirty percent intensity. That's the whole look.
Then sound design: music ducking, a few whooshes, and a loudness pass to minus fourteen LUFS.
The real speed trick is batching: I edit three videos in one sitting, so I stay in the same mindset.
Finally I export with the YouTube preset and do one full watch-through before uploading. Thanks for watching.
